contract: Feed identical contiguous windows to the dca parser with default flags and to Dts14SyncReader::per_frame, Dts14CarrierReader or DtsNormalSourceReader as named by argument one. Argument two gives the input packing and argument three the byte window.

Fold kind 1 with physical packet offset, byte count, sample rate, coded duration in samples per channel, and all source bytes. Candidate rate and duration are source header facts, zero where unavailable. The reference reports its parser clock.
Fold kind 7 for clean EOF or kind 8 for a refusal. The sync reader's canonical output is compared to the packing oracle on the byte-exact geometry cases.
Preload input and parse arguments before the operation. Setup, framing, byte folding, and teardown are inside it.

open_deviations.reading: A source that ends inside a header or a word
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.4.2: the header is 104 bits, 120 with HCRC; a word packing stores whole 16-bit words, and a 14-bit word carries its payload in the low 14 bits (TS 102 114 V1.2.1 clause 5.3)
open_deviations.candidate: refuses with Truncated where the source ends inside a header or a 16-bit source word, after every complete frame
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser flushes the remaining bytes as a packet, odd bytes included, with no clock or the header's clock
open_deviations.compat: a consumer that wants the incomplete tail passed on, as the reference does, would use a compat::dts policy that returns it as an incomplete frame (not built)

open_deviations.reading: A stream that does not begin with a normal core sync
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clauses 5.3 and 7.2: a core frame begins with SYNC 0x7FFE8001 followed by FTYPE 1 and SHORT 31; an extension substream sync word is not a core frame
open_deviations.candidate: refuses with Invalid: the stream does not start with a normal sync, as the reader documents it must
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns the bytes as a packet with no clock

open_deviations.reading: Header codes the specification rules out
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.4.2: SFREQ 0, 4, 5, 9, 10, 14 and 15 (Table 5-5), RATE other than 0 to 24 and 29 (Table 5-7), LFF 3 (Table 5-14) and PCMR 4 and 7 (Table 5-17) are invalid, FSIZE 0 to 94 and NBLKS 0 to 4 are invalid, a normal frame has SHORT 31 (Table 5-3) and NBLKS 7, 15, 31, 63 or 127, and FixedBit is 0
open_deviations.candidate: refuses with Unsupported: SHORT 0 in a normal frame is neither a normal sync nor a termination frame
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns the frame's bytes as a packet with no clock

open_deviations.reading: Coded clock of arrangements the parser has no layout for
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.4.2: SFREQ gives the core sampling frequency (Table 5-5) and NBLKS a window of 32 x (NBLKS + 1) samples, 256 to 4096 in a normal frame, whatever AMODE says; AMODE 10 to 15 are defined arrangements and 16 to 63 user defined (Table 5-4)
open_deviations.candidate: reports the rate and duration SFREQ and NBLKS code: 48000 Hz with 512 samples, or 256 samples for NBLKS 7
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns the same bytes with a zero rate and duration

open_deviations.reading: Coded facts of a header with an invalid field
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.4.2: SFREQ codes the rate (Table 5-5, codes 0, 4, 5, 9, 10, 14 and 15 invalid) and NBLKS 5 to 127 a window of 32 x (NBLKS + 1) samples, independently of the other fields
open_deviations.candidate: reports the coded SFREQ rate and 32 x (NBLKS + 1) samples of the span, zero for a code without a value, without judging the other fields, as the reader documents
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns the same bytes with no clock, or with 96000 or 192000 Hz for SFREQ 14 and 15

open_deviations.reading: Clock of a final frame shorter than FSIZE + 1
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.4.2: SFREQ and NBLKS in a complete header code the frame's rate and window; FSIZE + 1 is its full size
open_deviations.candidate: returns the final span of whole words with its header's 48000 Hz and 512 samples; the span is shorter than FSIZE + 1 bytes
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns the same bytes with no clock

open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.4.2: every frame header codes SFREQ, the core sampling frequency of that frame (Table 5-5), and NBLKS, its window of 32 x (NBLKS + 1) samples
open_deviations.candidate: reports each frame's own rate and 32 x (NBLKS + 1) samples
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser keeps the first frame's rate and rescales later durations (557, 470, 1115 and 768 samples)
open_deviations.compat: a consumer that needs one stream-wide rate, as the reference publishes, would use a compat::dts policy that latches the first frame's rate (not built)

open_deviations.reading: Clock of a packet that ends in half a word

open_deviations.candidate: returns the 113-byte packet with no clock: it does not unpack to one whole frame
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns the same bytes with the header's 44100 Hz and 1024 samples

open_deviations.reading: Frames whose physical lengths differ from one another
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.3: every frame begins with the 38-bit extended sync, SYNC with FTYPE 1 and SHORT 31
open_deviations.candidate: returns one frame per normal sync, each from its sync to the next (128 + 128, 112 + 160 and 112 + 128 + 160 bytes)
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns all frames as one packet (256, 272 or 400 bytes) with no clock

open_deviations.reading: 14-bit frames whose canonical length is not determined
open_deviations.clause: ETSI TS 102 114 V1.6.1 clause 5.4.2: FSIZE + 1 is the frame's size in bytes; TS 102 114 V1.2.1 clause 5.3: a 14-bit stream carries it in the low 14 bits of each word
open_deviations.candidate: refuses with Unsupported: the canonical frame cannot be fixed exactly from a nonzero tail or a competing FSIZE reading, as the sync reader documents
open_deviations.reference: the dca parser returns the physical bytes as a packet with the header's clock; it has no canonical step, and the carrier and normal readers return the same packets
